questions.question: Which type of intellectual property primarily protects original software source code and documentation?
questions.option_a: A. Patent
questions.option_b: B. Copyright
questions.option_c: C. Trademark
questions.option_d: D. Trade secret only
questions.explanation: Copyrights protect original works of authorship including software code and documentation.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of data privacy principles in IT?
questions.option_a: A. To generate government revenue
questions.option_b: B. To protect individuals’ personal information from unauthorized access or misuse
questions.option_c: C. To restrict all internet usage
questions.option_d: D. To protect only corporate trade secrets
questions.explanation: Data privacy focuses on safeguarding personal data, respecting individuals’ rights, and ensuring responsible handling.

questions.question: Which software license type makes the source code available but requires compliance with specific terms such as GPL, MIT or Apache?
questions.option_a: A. Proprietary
questions.option_b: B. Freeware
questions.option_c: C. Open-Source
questions.option_d: D. Shareware
questions.explanation: Open-source licenses provide source code access while imposing conditions that must be followed.

questions.question: In the Uber 2016 data breach, the main legal and ethical concerns involved:
questions.option_a: A. Only patent infringement
questions.option_b: B. Data protection, breach notification duties, and the ethical responsibility to protect users and remain transparent
questions.option_c: C. Trademark misuse only
questions.option_d: D. Failure to use open-source software
questions.explanation: The incident highlighted cybersecurity obligations, notification requirements and ethical duties of transparency and protection.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a core value of the CSSL Code of Ethics?
questions.option_a: A. Professionalism
questions.option_b: B. Honesty
questions.option_c: C. Maximizing shareholder profit regardless of consequences
questions.option_d: D. Responsibility and Integrity
questions.explanation: CSSL core values are Professionalism, Honesty, Competence, Professional Development, Adding Value to Sri Lanka, and Responsibility and Integrity.

questions.question: A software license primarily defines:
questions.option_a: A. Only the hardware requirements of the program
questions.option_b: B. Who can use the software, how it may be used, copied, modified and distributed
questions.option_c: C. The programming language used
questions.option_d: D. The physical size of the installation media
questions.explanation: Licenses specify usage rights, copying, modification and distribution conditions.

questions.question: Which regulatory standard is specifically associated with protecting payment card data in the finance sector?
questions.option_a: A. HIPAA
questions.option_b: B. PCI-DSS
questions.option_c: C. TRCSL
questions.option_d: D. GPL
questions.explanation: PCI-DSS is the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard used in finance.

questions.question: What does the ‘Access Right’ ethical issue mainly address?
questions.option_a: A. Only physical building security
questions.option_b: B. Who may access systems and data, the permissions they hold, and prevention of unauthorized access
questions.option_c: C. Marketing access to customers
questions.option_d: D. Open-source code availability
questions.explanation: Access rights cover authorized access, least-privilege permissions, access controls (passwords, MFA, RBAC) and monitoring balanced with privacy.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a harmful action in IT ethics?
questions.option_a: A. Applying security patches regularly
questions.option_b: B. Spreading malware or intentionally destroying data
questions.option_c: C. Using strong authentication
questions.option_d: D. Documenting system changes
questions.explanation: Harmful actions include spreading malware, destroying data, unauthorized system alteration and causing disruption.

questions.question: Trade secrets in IT typically include:
questions.option_a: A. Publicly published open-source code
questions.option_b: B. Confidential source code, unique algorithms, business strategies and unreleased R&D
questions.option_c: C. Registered trademarks only
questions.option_d: D. Freeware applications
questions.explanation: Trade secrets are confidential information that gives a competitive advantage and is not publicly known.

questions.question: A major ethical challenge of AI systems highlighted in the lecture is:
questions.option_a: A. They always eliminate all human jobs immediately
questions.option_b: B. Bias and fairness when trained on biased historical data
questions.option_c: C. They never require human oversight
questions.option_d: D. They cannot be used in recruitment
questions.explanation: AI can produce discriminatory outcomes if trained on biased data; transparency, human responsibility and safety are also key concerns.

questions.question: In the Cambridge Analytica / Facebook case, the primary ethical failing was:
questions.option_a: A. Using open-source software without attribution
questions.option_b: B. Lack of transparency and misuse of personal data without informed consent
questions.option_c: C. Patent infringement
questions.option_d: D. Failure to apply security patches
questions.explanation: Personal data were obtained and used for political profiling without users’ informed understanding, raising privacy, consent and trust issues.

questions.question: The Amazon AI recruitment tool case illustrated which ethical problem?
questions.option_a: A. Copyright violation of training data
questions.option_b: B. Gender bias resulting from historical hiring data
questions.option_c: C. Use of proprietary software without license
questions.option_d: D. Physical security breaches
questions.explanation: The system showed bias against women because it learned from past male-dominated hiring patterns.

questions.question: Pratibha Syntex was penalized for:
questions.option_a: A. Data breach notification failure
questions.option_b: B. Using unlicensed Microsoft and Adobe software
questions.option_c: C. AI bias in hiring
questions.option_d: D. Violating GDPR only
questions.explanation: The company settled a copyright and software-licensing case for $100,000 after using pirated software.

questions.question: Which Sri Lankan law provides legal recognition for electronic contracts and e-signatures?
questions.option_a: A. Computer Crime Act No. 24 of 2007
questions.option_b: B. Electronic Transactions Act No. 19 of 2006
questions.option_c: C. CSSL Code of Ethics
questions.option_d: D. TRCSL regulations only
questions.explanation: The Electronic Transactions Act No. 19 of 2006 gives legal validity to electronic contracts and signatures in Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Freeware is best described as:
questions.option_a: A. Software whose source code must always be published under GPL
questions.option_b: B. Software that is free to use but whose source code is not necessarily open
questions.option_c: C. Software that requires payment after a trial period
questions.option_d: D. Fully proprietary software with no free version
questions.explanation: Freeware can be used without payment, but the source code may remain closed.

questions.question: Shareware typically means:
questions.option_a: A. Completely free and open-source software
questions.option_b: B. A trial version that requires payment for full features
questions.option_c: C. Software owned by the government
questions.option_d: D. Software that cannot be modified under any circumstances
questions.explanation: Shareware provides a limited trial; full functionality usually requires a license fee.

questions.question: Which best practice is listed for IT professionals in the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Never update software to avoid compatibility issues
questions.option_b: B. Strong passwords & authentication, regular backups, security patches, access control and compliance
questions.option_c: C. Sharing all passwords among team members for convenience
questions.option_d: D. Ignoring data-protection laws if the company is small
questions.explanation: Best practices include strong authentication, backups, updates, cybersecurity awareness, access control, privacy protection, documentation and legal compliance.

questions.question: Under the CSSL Code of Ethics, ‘Competence’ requires professionals to:
questions.option_a: A. Accept any project regardless of skill level
questions.option_b: B. Accept only work they are qualified to perform and continuously improve their knowledge
questions.option_c: C. Never share knowledge with others
questions.option_d: D. Focus solely on profit
questions.explanation: Competence means taking only work one is qualified for, lifelong learning and delivering quality services.

questions.question: The ‘Adding Value to Sri Lanka’ principle of the CSSL Code emphasizes:
questions.option_a: A. Using ICT only for personal gain
questions.option_b: B. Using ICT to improve society, support national digital transformation and develop solutions for national development
questions.option_c: C. Avoiding any contribution to local projects
questions.option_d: D. Exporting all software without local benefit
questions.explanation: This value encourages ICT professionals to contribute to Sri Lanka’s social and economic development.

questions.question: In the Priya ‘Helpful Developer’ case study, the primary legal issue is:
questions.option_a: A. Unauthorized access to customer data
questions.option_b: B. Use of proprietary software without proper licenses (copyright infringement)
questions.option_c: C. AI bias in the project
questions.option_d: D. Failure to report a data breach
questions.explanation: The company is using proprietary tools without purchasing licenses, which violates copyright and software-licensing law.

questions.question: What ethical dilemma does Priya face in the case study?
questions.option_a: A. Whether to delete customer data
questions.option_b: B. Pressure to deliver results quickly versus the obligation to respect intellectual property and professional integrity
questions.option_c: C. Whether to open-source the entire product
questions.option_d: D. Whether to ignore cybersecurity patches
questions.explanation: She knows the use of unlicensed software is illegal yet faces managerial pressure and team delivery deadlines.

questions.question: In the Data Breach Dilemma case, the CEO’s desire to hide the breach primarily violates:
questions.option_a: A. Only trademark law
questions.option_b: B. Legal breach-notification duties and ethical principles of transparency, honesty and responsibility to customers
questions.option_c: C. Open-source license terms
questions.option_d: D. Patent filing requirements
questions.explanation: Hiding a breach that exposed personal data breaches both legal notification obligations and CSSL values of honesty and responsibility.

questions.question: Which step of the ETHICAL decision-making framework involves identifying the people or parties affected by the decision?
questions.option_a: A. E – Evaluate the situation
questions.option_b: B. T – Think about stakeholders
questions.option_c: C. H – Highlight legal requirements
questions.option_d: D. L – Learn and reflect
questions.explanation: ‘T – Think about stakeholders’ requires consideration of everyone impacted by the decision.

questions.question: An IT consultant is offered a lucrative contract by a competitor that requires using knowledge developed for the current client (no non-compete signed). Which CSSL value is most directly at risk?
questions.option_a: A. Adding Value to Sri Lanka
questions.option_b: B. Responsibility and Integrity (protecting confidential information and avoiding conflicts of interest)
questions.option_c: C. Professional Development only
questions.option_d: D. Competence in programming languages
questions.explanation: Using a client’s confidential techniques for a competitor creates a conflict of interest and risks disclosure of trade secrets.

questions.question: For a cash-strapped Sri Lankan startup building an educational app, which database choice is generally most suitable from a licensing and cost perspective?
questions.option_a: A. A proprietary commercial database with high annual fees
questions.option_b: B. MySQL under the GPL open-source license
questions.option_c: C. Any freeware database that prohibits commercial use
questions.option_d: D. A closed-source database that cannot be modified
questions.explanation: MySQL (GPL) is free to use, source is available, and is widely accepted for commercial applications when license terms are respected.

questions.question: VS Code is distributed under which type of license?
questions.option_a: A. Proprietary closed-source
questions.option_b: B. Open-source MIT license
questions.option_c: C. Shareware requiring payment after 30 days
questions.option_d: D. GPL only
questions.explanation: VS Code is open-source under the MIT license, allowing free use, modification and distribution with minimal restrictions.

questions.question: Adobe Creative Cloud is an example of:
questions.option_a: A. Open-source software
questions.option_b: B. Proprietary software requiring a subscription license
questions.option_c: C. Freeware with unrestricted modification rights
questions.option_d: D. Public-domain software
questions.explanation: Adobe Creative Cloud is proprietary; use is governed by a paid subscription license with restrictions on copying and redistribution.

questions.question: Which statement about open-source software is FALSE?
questions.option_a: A. Source code is available
questions.option_b: B. It can never be used for commercial purposes
questions.option_c: C. Specific license terms (GPL, MIT, Apache) must be followed
questions.option_d: D. Modification is often permitted under the license
questions.explanation: Many open-source licenses explicitly allow commercial use provided the license conditions are met.

questions.question: Electronic signatures in Sri Lanka:
questions.option_a: A. Have no legal recognition
questions.option_b: B. Can have legal validity under the Electronic Transactions Act
questions.option_c: C. Are valid only for government contracts
questions.option_d: D. Require physical ink to be valid
questions.explanation: The Electronic Transactions Act No. 19 of 2006 grants legal recognition to electronic signatures when proper conditions are satisfied.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct statement about regulatory compliance?
questions.option_a: A. It is optional for small IT companies
questions.option_b: B. Failure to comply can result in fines, legal action and reputational damage
questions.option_c: C. It only applies to hardware manufacturers
questions.option_d: D. It replaces the need for ethical behaviour
questions.explanation: Regulatory compliance protects customers and the organization; non-compliance carries significant legal and business risks.

questions.question: HIPAA is the regulatory framework primarily concerned with:
questions.option_a: A. Payment card data
questions.option_b: B. Healthcare data privacy and security
questions.option_c: C. Telecommunications licensing in Sri Lanka
questions.option_d: D. Open-source software distribution
questions.explanation: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) governs the protection of personal health information.

questions.question: TRCSL is the regulatory body relevant to which sector in Sri Lanka?
questions.option_a: A. Healthcare only
questions.option_b: B. Telecommunications
questions.option_c: C. Banking card payments
questions.option_d: D. Software patent examination
questions.explanation: TRCSL (Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka) regulates the telecom sector.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates the CSSL value of Honesty?
questions.option_a: A. Claiming sole credit for a team project
questions.option_b: B. Being truthful in professional work, avoiding plagiarism and giving proper credit
questions.option_c: C. Hiding a known security vulnerability to protect reputation
questions.option_d: D. Using unlicensed software to meet a deadline
questions.explanation: Honesty requires truthfulness, avoidance of deception and proper attribution of others’ work.

questions.question: A key difference between proprietary and open-source software is:
questions.option_a: A. Proprietary software is always free
questions.option_b: B. Proprietary software is owned by a company with restrictions on use, modification and sharing; open-source makes source code available under license terms
questions.option_c: C. Open-source software cannot be used commercially
questions.option_d: D. Proprietary software always provides source code
questions.explanation: Proprietary licenses restrict use and modification; open-source licenses grant access to source code under defined conditions.

questions.question: When applying the ETHICAL framework, the step ‘H – Highlight legal requirements’ requires the professional to:
questions.option_a: A. Ignore all laws if they conflict with business goals
questions.option_b: B. Identify and understand the relevant laws, regulations and contractual obligations that apply to the situation
questions.option_c: C. Focus only on ethical principles and never on law
questions.option_d: D. Delay any decision until all laws worldwide are reviewed
questions.explanation: This step ensures the decision is grounded in applicable legal obligations before ethical principles are applied.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the ethical stance on collecting user data to improve products when users do not fully understand how the data will be used?
questions.option_a: A. Always ethical because product improvement benefits everyone
questions.option_b: B. Raises serious privacy and transparency concerns; informed consent and clear communication are required
questions.option_c: C. Irrelevant because data collection is never regulated
questions.option_d: D. Acceptable only for open-source projects
questions.explanation: Ethical data practices require transparency, informed consent and respect for privacy even when the goal is product improvement.

questions.question: In a scenario where an IT professional discovers a data breach three months after it occurred, the ethically and legally preferred course of action is:
questions.option_a: A. Quietly fix the vulnerability and never inform customers
questions.option_b: B. Notify affected customers and relevant authorities as required, remediate the issue, and improve security practices
questions.option_c: C. Delete all logs to erase evidence
questions.option_d: D. Wait until the next annual report to mention it
questions.explanation: Both legal notification duties and ethical principles of honesty, responsibility and protection of individuals require timely disclosure and remediation.

questions.question: Which statement about personal liability of IT professionals for data breaches is most accurate in the context of the lecture and tutorial?
questions.option_a: A. IT professionals can never be held personally responsible
questions.option_b: B. Personal liability may arise if the professional acted negligently, violated professional codes, or ignored known security obligations
questions.option_c: C. Only the CEO is ever liable
questions.option_d: D. Liability is automatic for every employee in the IT department
questions.explanation: While organizational liability is primary, individual professionals can face consequences for negligence, code-of-ethics violations or deliberate misconduct.

questions.question: When choosing an operating system for a cost-sensitive educational startup in Sri Lanka, Ubuntu is often preferred over Windows because:
questions.option_a: A. Ubuntu is proprietary and more secure
questions.option_b: B. Ubuntu is open-source, free of license fees, and allows modification and redistribution under its license
questions.option_c: C. Windows is open-source
questions.option_d: D. Ubuntu cannot run educational software
questions.explanation: Ubuntu (and similar Linux distributions) eliminate proprietary licensing costs and provide the freedom typical of open-source software.

questions.question: The ‘L – Learn and reflect’ step of the ETHICAL framework emphasizes:
questions.option_a: A. Never changing one’s decision after acting
questions.option_b: B. Reviewing the outcome of the decision, learning from the experience, and improving future ethical decision-making
questions.option_c: C. Documenting only successful outcomes
questions.option_d: D. Ignoring stakeholder feedback
questions.explanation: Reflection closes the decision cycle and builds professional ethical competence over time.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct application of the CSSL principle of Professional Development?
questions.option_a: A. Refusing to learn new technologies after graduation
questions.option_b: B. Keeping up with emerging technologies, engaging in lifelong learning, and sharing knowledge
questions.option_c: C. Avoiding any professional certifications
questions.option_d: D. Focusing solely on current job tasks without broader learning
questions.explanation: Professional Development requires continuous learning and knowledge sharing within the ICT community.

questions.question: In the context of access control, role-based permissions mean:
questions.option_a: A. Every user receives administrator rights
questions.option_b: B. Users are granted only the access rights necessary for their specific job roles (least privilege)
questions.option_c: C. Access is never monitored
questions.option_d: D. Passwords are shared among all employees
questions.explanation: Role-based access control implements the principle of least privilege, reducing the risk of unauthorized actions.

questions.question: Which real-world case best illustrates the legal and ethical risks of using unlicensed proprietary software?
questions.option_a: A. Cambridge Analytica
questions.option_b: B. Pratibha Syntex
questions.option_c: C. Amazon AI recruitment
questions.option_d: D. Uber 2016 breach
questions.explanation: Pratibha Syntex settled a copyright infringement case after using unlicensed Microsoft and Adobe software.

questions.question: A professional who accepts a project outside their area of competence primarily violates which CSSL core value?
questions.option_a: A. Adding Value to Sri Lanka
questions.option_b: B. Competence
questions.option_c: C. Professionalism only in appearance
questions.option_d: D. Honesty about project deadlines
questions.explanation: Competence requires accepting only work one is qualified to perform and delivering quality outcomes.
